newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Kvaerner planning to buy shipyards in China, India.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner planning to buy shipyards in China, India.

text.p: Norwegian shipbuilding and engineering giant Kvaerner said on Thursday it plans to acquire two shipbuilding firms in China or India in an effort to raise Asian revenues.

"We are looking at investment opportunity in shipbuilding for Asia and I think possibly this year or next year you will see the first shipbuilding engagement for us in Asia," president and chief executive Erik Toenseth told a news conference.
He said the company was seeking "to acquire wholly or partially shipyards" in either or both China or India for their large home markets as long-term commitments.
Kvaerner expects Asia's 40 percent contribution to the group's estimated US$10 billion turnover in 1997 to rise to 50 percent next year.
Kvaerner is Europe's largest builder of cruise ships and specialised ships such as cable layers and gas carriers.
Its high end niche market, Toenseth said, was not in direct competition with Asian shipyards which generally build bulk carriers and tankers.

He said Asian revenues would also be rise because Kvaerner's acquisition of U.K. conglomerate Trafalgar House put it in a strong position to bid for turnkey contracts in Asia for the construction of oil refineries and petrochemical plants.
Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Australia are the company's more important oil and gas markets in Asia, said Raymond Carlsen, president of the Singapore unit.
Kvaerner announced on December 27 it had won a $420 million turnkey contract for the world's largest production barge from Australian oil company Woodside Offshore Petroleum.
Carlsen said the company was also focusing on the regional pulp and paper and hydropower business.

Kvaerner officially opened its regional operations office in Singapore on Thursday. The office has been granted operational headquarters status by the Singapore government, which gives it some tax breaks.
Singapore is already Kvaerner's worldwide headquarters for its ship equipment business.
